title: On Becoming a Guinea Fowl
review: Fascinating portrait of modern subsaharan Africa. All of life’s first world amenities, AirPods, cars, computers, copy machines, cellphones, zoom calls, social media, and vertical video are placed directly alongside old and seemly outdated traditions. There is still malaria nets, charcoal men, unsophisticated police procedures, and sweeping horrible crimes under the rug to preserved the image of an unbroken family. Not that these issues are endemic to Africa or anything, you find a lot of the same problems everywhere else in world, especially as the world becomes more globalized. This is seen in the language too, you get lots of phrases and sometimes even full scenes in English but the entire movie is subtitled because the characters jumps between dialects so frequently. It’s like the new generation is adapting to the new world while struggling to hold on to their traditions for better or worse. It’s this dichotomy and divide between the younger and older generations that make this movie say more than just what’s presented to you.

Theaters how we know it is going away, and despite a lot of people’s and my own best efforts I don’t think there is much we can do about it. It’ll still exist sure but it’s gonna be a lot different, and in all these senses Netflix deserves some blame. But the reality is a movie like Train Dreams while beautiful and cinematic and deserving to be viewed on a big screen, just isn’t viable in this day and age. Who would go see this in theaters? Pretty much no one. So I guess it’s a good thing that Netflix will still make movies like this and put them in a place for audiences to see, but when I watch the end of this on my phone screen I can’t help but feel I’m watching the monster and not the little boy.

title: Bugonia
review: Yorgos has long been a mystery to me. The Killing of a Sacred Deer, the Lobster and Poor Things are all very different movies, but if there is one thing that unites them it’s that they clearly take place in a world that is not ours. They are different realities constructed to act as the setting for bizarre stories. Now the stories often act as metaphors for our just as bizarre societal rituals like jobs, dating and sex. With Bugonia, Yorgos taps into what he started with. Which is the kind of crazy that we really see in our world. Messed up families like the ones in Dogtooth, who despite clearly being crazy you still believe people like this are out there blending into our world.  Their plan is simple enough to work, the cops are dumb enough to let it happen. Their theories, while crazy, we’ve maybe heard before and are such good motifs for the ultra rich that you start to think maybe it’s not as crazy as he seems. It’s this kind of realism that I appreciate from a film, and it’s the kind that Yorgos has lacked since Dogtooth. But the real beauty of this movie and movies in general is that once he has done all this setup, he completely turns it on its head at the end to hammer home his message. I loved it 5 stars.

Scarlett's character is I believe named Zola or something  else with a Z. Probably because her publicist or this movie's branding team thought it would make her stand out, but she doesn't in the slightest. She is the most shallow protagonist, her job is 'illegal doer' her backstory is 'friend died' her motive is ~~'movie~~' sorry 'money.'  She doesn't grow, struggle with morality or tough decisions she barley exists. The movie takes a full hour to get to 'oh no we are standing on an island with dinosaurs' which is where we all knew it was going anyway so taking that long to get there and with non stop terrible character work and bland world building its just no acceptable from an enjoyment perspective. The one nice thing I have to say about this movie is that it looks mostly fantastic, but that just makes it even more disappointing because it makes you yearn for even a respectable story and that's just not what you get here. God I could go on forever about all the things wrong with this movie but I'll 2 leave it with 2 more backhanded compliments. The one character saying 'I wonder if when and old person buys a new bed, they think to themselves "this is my deathbed"' was a great line undercut by the fact that the character then explains it and then another character says 'we get it' And the professors rant about how intelligence isn't necessarily a great survival trait was fantastic and I can't believe they wasted a speech so good in the middle of a movie so awful.

Ken is just Ken. He is a happy in-between of the nonsensical humor of Barbieland the actual movie stuff. Other than that I really enjoyed it Greta delivered a funny and thoughtful movie from a tough concept and I think it deserves praise.

title: Nope
review:
5 star review of Nope I wrote at work cause I was bored.

1st star – The filmmaking. Peele has proven time and again that he an excellent eye for great shots. With the kind of buzz that his name generates now it great to see him be able to fully realize his vision and create elaborate set pieces.

2nd star – The premise. My favorite premise of the year. Everyone has seen the blurry uninspiring UAP videos the pentagon has released by now and while it doesn’t at all prove that aliens are among us, it does make me curious. Peele plays beautifully on this curiosity as well as dipping into the fear aspect of it. The main characters being descendants of the very first movie star is also a great detail, especially for capturing another groundbreaking feat like a UFO on film. 

3rd star – The characters. They are fun, smart and motivated. Even the minor characters play a part. OJ is an infamous name now especially in Hollywood, and Peele knows exactly how to use it.

4th star – The horror. Not much to be said without spoiling but there are 2 scene that are a different type of horror and I loved it. Also some nice misdirection with classic horror and tension elements. 

5th star – The metaphor. Peele’s principal metaphor between Gordy’s and Jean Jacket is just fantastic. There are a couple ways to interoperate it but I like this one. The table cloth that hides Steven Yeun’s eyes from Gordy is the real thing that saved his life and the movie uses this to draw parallels between the two animals. It’s this idea that a less intelligent being won’t attack until it can see the danger. Peele is showing that when it comes to extraterrestrial threats we are the less intelligent being. The alien could be right in front of us hiding with an illusion like behind a tablecloth or a cloud but because we can see it we don't fear it. Its like the trick that owners like to play on their dogs where they throw up a bedsheet and the run away to be amused how the dog reacts. This movie proposes the idea that what if aliens are doing the same thing to us. We are not more intelligent to them than an ape, horse or dog is to us. It just so rich and so different from most themes in movies I loved it.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Film Class Essay:

Bradley Cooper’s Nightmare Performance 

Guillermo Del Toro’s 2021 film “Nightmare Alley” is a beautifully shot and directed movie. However, this is as far as I am willing to praise the film especially in comparison to the original 1947 version. Despite a longer runtime the “Nightmare Alley” remake fails to create as compelling a story and thematic arc as the original, but where the movie especially falls flat is in the acting performances. Bradley Cooper plays main character Stan Carlisle, but Cooper fails to deliver the same power that Tyrone Power brought to the character 84 years earlier.   

“Nightmare Alley” begins similar to the original, and Cooper adequately plays Stan in the first act. In the original at the end of the first act Stan has a moment where he successfully cons a police officer away from shutting down the carnival. This is a turning point for Stan as he realizes he is no longer the naïve student that falls for Pete’s (played by David Strathairn) basic reads. However, due to slight changes in the script and more manic performance Cooper never finds this transformation. Because of this as the movie goes on Cooper comes off as a naïve and unconvincing con man instead of the cunning and suave socialite that Power portrayed.   

The scene where you can see this change is when Stan first meets Cate Blanchett’s character, Dr. Lilith Ritter. In the original Stan correctly guesses that Dr. Ritter is trying to fool him by making up a dead relative. This is a smart and satisfying moment as the experienced Stan shows he knows what to do with a mysterious woman at one of his shows. Del Toro’s version alters this scene dramatically though. What happens instead is that Stan correctly predicts that Dr. Ritter has a gun with an ivory handle in her handbag. This description is so accurate that when it is proved correct it completely ruins the credibility of the movie. Stan is supposed to be a smart and experienced con man, not an all-knowing God. The film tries to play this off the same way as Stan understanding how the world works, but it’s done in an inferior and unbelievable way. 

This problem is only exasperated when the movie introduces its next diversion from the original. Surprise! Ezra Grindle isn’t just a skeptical rich guy that misses his daughter, he’s a reclusive mob boss who is so concerned about his secrets so much that he invented the lie detector test. Despite looking physically nervous and stuttering the entire time Cooper apparently passes this test. It seems like Stan is just the luckiest man in the world, no wonder the whole movie Cooper gives off this “awe shucks golly gee” attitude. The performance at this point is completely different from the 1947 version. Cooper portrays Stan as in way over his head, instead of in control of his biggest score yet. This is a fine decision in a vacuum however, the issue with this change is that it takes away from the final reveal of the movie. 

In the original version Stan muses about how a man could become The Geek saying, “I don’t know how a man gets that low.” We see Stan get that low himself after he is so infatuated by his own greed and power that he takes advantage of grieving relatives for money. This shady behavior leads to him being run out of town and becoming a geek level drunk. While all these same plot points happen in the new version is feels less earned because Bradley Cooper never portrays Stan as a villain. Thus the beautiful thematic arc that Stan went through in the original in ruined by a meddled with script and a confused performance.

title: The Act of Killing
review:
Film class review:

The Act of Killing is undoubtedly one of the most perplexing documentaries and film in general that I've ever seen. This has to do mostly with the extreme differences in history, culture, and governing between the United States and Indonesia. The constant emphasis on gangsters as "Free Men" and not criminals is a perfect example. Indonesia sees its past as a necessary evil that is even celebrated in order to maintain the status quo. The government is also perfectly fine with letting the perpetrators of their genocides get of scot free because most of them became leaders in the government. The cultural differences is also jarring, and this is especially evident with the ritual dancing juxtaposed with reenactment of the village massacre. The two acts are almost seen in same light, both honoring past events and culture. Through the eyes of an uniformed this seems grotesque, but in Indonesia they have been living this way for 60 years now.

Its fitting that the director's last name of this film is Oppenheimer because he dropped a nuclear bomb on traditional documentary filmmaking. The use of reenactments is totally different in this film from what we have seen in previous viewings. In "The Thin Blue Line" the reenactments are done by actors the directed to recreate the truth as accurately as possible, but in "The Act of Killing" these reenactments are done by the people who committed these horrendous crimes. It is such an interesting and confounding tool of self reflection; I can't imagine why most of these people have agreed to do this or why they don't feel more guilt. It really makes you question what kind of environment makes become this way and is a true testament to the power of documentary filmmaking. While tragic this film shows an entirely new perspective and style to me and that is the essence of what a great documentary film should do.  

Finally the ending of this film must be discussed. Whether its acting of a truthful reflex of disgust and shame it really makes the viewer question what human beings are really capable of doing. Anwar Congo seems to have a moment of true reflection and sorrow, but does that forgive his past crimes? The mastery of this film is that it makes Anwar out to be the ultimate badass and evil figure but at the end he is reduced to a sympathetic character that it's hard to not momentarily feel a little pity for. The real tragedy is that Anwar's roots were not even all that sinister, just a movie ticket scalper forced to commit heinous acts because of the state of his country.

title: Born into Brothels: Calcutta's Red Light Kids
review:
Zana Briski and Ross Kauffman's "Born Into Brothels" is one of the more uplifting documentaries we have watched this semester. Despite the harsh conditions of the Red Light District which they show off in a variety of ways weather it be the opening shot of rats or the shot of a child chained to a fence; I can't help but come away from this documentary with feelings of hope and goodness. 

A really interesting component of the movie for me was the comparison made between the children and the zoo animals. Much like how the zoo animals eat all the plastic they are fed because they don't know better, the children fail to grasp what such a harsh upbringing and no education can do to their lives. The film actually shows very few moments of the truly terrible conditions of the brothels and the abuse they take from their parents, but focuses more on the uplifting aspects of Zana's help. The children's photos do more to tell the conditions they live in than any of the film shot by the directors. As Avijit says "That's why I like photography, I want to put across the behavior of man." I thought this was a very mature and polished quote from such a young child. The children's interviews go a long way to show the loss of innocence that growing up in the brothel can bring. The children act mature because they have too. Cooking, cleaning and making drunks pay for sex is just a part of their life that they have learned to accept. 

The film's uplifting tone still dominates the narrative though. The joy of the children seeing the ocean almost makes all the suffering worth it and lets the kids act like children again. The bus ride home with the beautiful music and blurry slow motion dancing of the children captures a moment of pure elation in the dirty and destitute pleasure seeking world. Appreciating the happiness these kids are experiencing given this opportunity that they would otherwise not have is the true beauty of this film. "Don’t Carry the Weight of the World on Your Shoulders, Just the Weight of This Moment."

The directors commitment to the kids it what really elevates this documentary. As someone who recently went thorough the process of getting their license and passport renewed, I can understand the immense effort it must have taken for the directors to try and get all the paperwork in order for these children. Walls and walls of paper and documents, all handwritten with incorrect spellings and no authentication display how disorganized India is as a country; India is obviously extremely burdened by its massive population, and kids like Avijit and Kochi fall by the wayside. 

However this process along with the disillusion of Avijit to his reality still culminates in a happy ending. During the seen where the kids all have their blood drawn most of them act as expected, squirming and grimacing, except Avijit. He sits as still as a statue almost as he knows the results of the test before he even takes it. This along with the struggle to get him a passport make it seem he is headed for a tragic ending, but at the last minute a dream trip to Amsterdam saves him. Seeing him run around like a child snapping photos at the airport must have been a feeling of relief for the filmmakers and this feeling must have only amplified when he changed his mind about attending a better school.

Even with the mixed results from some of the children of finding them a batter life I can't help but feel this film achieved its goal and then some. She offered these kids something that otherwise would not have even been a possibility. As one of the kids said themselves "There is nothing called 'hope' in my future," but Briski and Kauffman offered them hope, even if it didn't work out for all of them. When the children are being taken to their new school we see their friendship and emotions a full display. One moment a friend crying on another's lap and the next singing and celebration. The smile and news that Kochi stayed in school makes me come away from this film with nothing but happiness.

title: Hoop Dreams
review:
Film class review:

One subtle aspect of Hoop Dreams that I appreciated was the establishing shots of Chicago. The slow zoom outs from the Willis Tower to various locations show that even though some of these neighborhoods are not that far geographically, they still differ greatly in economic status, safety and racial diversity. This stands out when the film shows Arthur's commute to St. Joe's at the beginning. He has to commute in the cold snowy weather on buses, trains, and by foot just to have a chance at his dream. The shot of Arthur's father buying drugs on the community basketball court also reinforces this idea of a divide between the boys basketball lives and their home lives. Basketball is an escape for them, and a path to a better life but even the courts at home aren't safe from dragging them back into the projects.

The most crushing moment in the whole movie for me is when William misses the two free throws to win the game vs St. Georges in the second semi finals match. The narrator had previously stated that William was always a clutch free throw shooter, but that aspect of his game failed him when he needed it most. Down by just one, and hobbled by his knee injury all William needed to do was make one of the free throws to force OT and extend St. Joe's chances, but he brutally and just barley missed both. This is an excruciating moment captured on video as it took all of Williams strength just to get back out there this season only for it to all fall on his shoulders. Plays like these demonstrate the extreme pressure that these boys are under not just from basketball but from the stress of trying to make it in the NBA to support their families. 

Another aspect of the film that was impactful was the filming of William's surgeries. Steve James and the other filmmakers are not afraid to show some slightly disturbing/stomach upsetting images from the surgery, but I feel as it is justified when you considered how important a player's knees are to basketball. These shots really show all the damage that a player's body can go through in the pursuit of becoming a professional athlete. It also shows all the man power and resources available through these programs; These players have all this to become the best that they possibly can whether it be though surgery or rehabilitation. 

The music is also fantastic, themes that feel right out of space jam backup the basketball and all the swagger on the screen. Rap music plays while Arthur and Shannon work at Pizza Hut. Dramatic and ominous music teems in the background during the ruthless recruitment camp. This music overall contributes to the feeling of the audience as it heightens the tensions in some scenes, and allows the audience to relax and enjoy a basketball montage in others.

title: The Thin Blue Line
review:
Errol Morris' "The Thin Blue Line" is another documentary that examines the justice system in America.

The use of reenactments to reveal details of the murder as they are presented in the interviews paints a murky picture of the crime and creates doubt in the viewers eyes. Morris only shows what is described in the interviews, and even changes it for each account. Even with all the subtle tweaks to the story, the reenactments have a certain authenticity to them because of the small consistencies like the driver fixing the rear view mirror when the officer approaches the car or the female officer throwing her malt out the car window. Morris also only presents the actual shooting only once when it if first described, all other times the screen fades to black and only the sound of a small caliber pistol firing can be heard. I think this is done to emphasize how weak the prosecutions case against Randall Adams really was. Even the Judge of the case admits that the primary reason Adams was even convicted was the closing argument of the prosecution about the "Thin Blue Line" that separates people from anarchy. Naming the film after this statement is a brilliant move by Morris because it shows how so often emotion and circumstances like Adams being in his thirties and David Harris being only 16 can contribute more weight to a sentencing than actual facts. 

Morris also uses several close ups in this movie. The first use of closeups on the back of the car shows how the female officer could have easily made the mistake between the 2 types of cars, but as the movie states you would hope a trained observer like her would be able to distinguish more. The Texas plates flash by in an instant and the car logos are so small that it is hard to blame the officer for losing the information in the hectic seconds after the shooting. What really stood out thought was the rear lights on the car, the difference between them is so stark up close yet on the shots of the two cars pulling after no time at all they fade into the same red lights. The other closeup in this movie is of the eyes of the Klu Klux Klan member from Vidor. This shot's meaning is more simple and is meant to show how corruption is still rampant in police departments along with the fact that only one officer from Vidor would help the defense with their case.

title: Grizzly Man
review:
Film Class Review:

Werner Herzog's Grizzly Man is a great documentary that shows the perspective of a film maker and explores the purpose of a documentary. 

One of the most interesting things about this movie is how it combines both footage that Herzog's shot along with Treadwell's own scenes. This allows the viewer to see the beauty of nature through the naïve eyes of an armature camera man and the experienced perspective that Herzog provides. Herzog also reinforces the perspective given many times throughout the movie that Timothy Treadwell got what was he was asking for. The first scene's framing really emphasizes this with how it seems like Treadwell is a safe distance from the bear in the shot but then he moves at the very end only to reveal another massive grizzly only a few yards behind him. This footage and the scene where the fox steals Treadwell's shoe are great examples how even though his intentions were good, he still acted like a helpless child among the animals. Despite the tragic ending Herzog is still able to craft a beautiful story from the tapes. The swings of emotion captured with the coming of rain, the moments of true introspection, and even the mad outbursts make Treadwell a truly sympathetic central character. Herzog's ability to tell such a compelling narrative and create a strong emotional heart from such a large volume of footage is something that only an experienced filmmaker like he could provide.

The other fascinating aspect of this documentary is it's purpose. It really feels like Herzog's intended to tell a story here the way the film was structured. Herzog is not making this movie because he wants to inform about grizzly bears or persuade to a certain side; He saw a human story and wanted to tell it. This is never more evident than when Herzog highlights the scene where the foxes join the shot along with the grizzly bears. Treadwell despite his faults had captured a truly amazing experience living among the bears, and it results in a story worth telling.

title: Dont Look Back
review:
Review for my film class

What stood out the most to me about this documentary was the way D. A. Pennebaker used the principal of "Show don't tell." My favorite example of this was when Bob Dylan was doing prep for the interview with the British African Society. The interviewer goes through the process of approving the questions with Dylan before starting, and Dylan's initial response to the questions almost says more than his actual answers would. When the interviewer finally asks his first question "How did you get your start?" Pennebaker cuts to Dylan singing in front of a small rural crowd showing his beginnings in folk music. This trick of indirectly answering the question through editing is one of my favorite parts of Pennebaker's style. Pennebaker uses "Show don't tell" several other times in the movie like with the character introductions of fellow artist Joan Baez, (When she spells her name for a reporter) and Dylan's manager Albert Grossman. Not using narration to introduce scene like in Primary gives Never Look Back a more authentic feel to me. Grossman's introduction of him yelling at a hotel manager is particularly amusing and probably the best laugh out loud moment of the film. These subtle scenes and clever cuts show while directors have less influence on observational documentaries, they still can have a strong impact on the final product.

title: Batman Ninja
review: Wow this was bad. I don't even know what to say it's just a mess in every aspect. The animation is decent sometimes, but never really commits fully to a style and looks super choppy even in between action scenes. The plot is laughable bad with random time jump, a ridiculous premise and way way way too many characters. Who makes this stuff.

title: North by Northwest
review: 3rd Hitchcock movie I've seen and this one was very classic. I still think he finds Cary Grant way more attractive than he really is but its always a joy to see him with Eva Marie Saint. Hitchcock's direction is fantastic they way he sets scenes and builds tension, especially strong during the dogfight. I still like Rear Window better but I can see this being one of Hitchcock's best.

title: Mistress America
review: Watched this again because it's so funny. Mamie-Claire is my favorite character but literally every line in this movie is hilarious. Mamie-Claire just lets all these people hang around in her house and also pisses Brooke off intentionally its so good.

title: It Comes at Night
review: The story was not very good and its not that scary, and all of the "horror" aspects of this movie are in dreams which is lame, especially for jump scares. The one cool thing about this movie though is what it does with the aspect ratio. They slowly compress it to increase tension and put you in the eyes of the main character, it's kinda genius. Trey Edwards Shults' subsequent movie "Waves" does a similar thing with using its aspect ratio and it's cool to see. Pretty well shot too, although some beats I think lingered a little too long.

title: The King and the Mockingbird
review: No fucking idea what I just watched or why, but hey I did.

title: Princess Mononoke
review: This movie is amazing I love how it looks. Themes of death and destruction but also hope and love, very complete story. Disturbing at times but also beautiful, I see why its one of the classic Studio Ghibli films.

title: Promising Young Woman
review: This is a decent movie with an important subject matter, but I think the execution and characters could have been a lot better and less one dimensional. Idk I guess I didn't like how every single guy is this story was discovered to be a total asshole (except the lawyer I guess) but that could just be the nice guy syndrome in me talking. There's some solid jokes/moments but overall I found it handled very strange, even with the story broken up into 5 parts. I think I'm being too harsh on this but I guess we'll see.

title: The Red Turtle
review: I want this movie to by my desktop background, every frame is so gorgeous.

title: Palm Springs
review: Watched this with my family, it's still pretty good on re-watch but I found myself enjoying it less the second time other than the beginning. Still a fun story with a good moments and realistic acting.

title: Safety Not Guaranteed
review: First movie of 2021 whoops. Yeah this is okay but it is not helped the the mixing of sci-fi and rom-com. Like the ending drags this down so much as they set up a decent story but it never fully commits to either, genre fully. Not bad thought has a couple intriguing moments.

title: Lady Bird
review:
Now this was awesome the second time watching it. Lady Bird is just such a fun protagonist and their are so many relatable moments in the story I love. Great mix of comedy and drama with an awesome cast and  heartwarming moments. 

The arm cast is such a cool feature to show the passage of time and symbolize her breaking her normal lifestyle. Greta Gerwig you are a genius.

title: Mistress America
review: One of the funniest movies I've watched in recent memory. Greta Gerwig is a fucking genius, the entire time they are in Connecticut is pure gold. So many great characters, funny lines, good shots and memorable moments. Def recommending this to everyone and coming back to it.

title: Nocturnal Animals
review: This was okay, watch it twice yesterday by pure coincidence but I was at least entertained both times. I still thing at it's heart half the story is just not all that interesting, Amy Adams character is just a dick to Jake the whole movie and I don't really connect to her at all besides not being able to sleep. The book content is the good part of the movie but even most of that has been done before.

title: Soul
review: This was very good. Prime Pixar, a movie with so much heart and New York style I loved it. Has a bunch of good laughs and best of all an original story. Pixar stop making Toy Story 7 or Finding the Pufferfish from Nemo or any of that other crap make more of these new and exciting ideas. Love the distinction the movie makes between a person's spark and their purpose, this movie is at it's best when its commenting of the fickle nature of life. Immediately one of my favorites of 2020.

title: Archenemy
review: This was okay. The first half of the movie is pretty good but it really struggles to put it all together in the end. The action is sub-par but at least the characters are memorable and his some decent styling. Creepy and cool at times but boring and predictable at others.

title: The Midnight Sky
review:
This movie: "Everyone on Earth is dead except George Clooney and this little girl"

Me: "Why?"

This movie: "Fuck you that's why"

title: Wonder Woman 1984
review: There was so much wrong with this I don't even know where to start. Okay I do, first of all 2 and half hours long? Why? Also, why are their also 2 villains? Hasn't Spider-Man 3 and The Amazing Spider-Man 2 proved that this is a bad idea. Pedro Pascal makes his character at least a little fun but his plan and the plot itself is so nonsensical it's unbelievable. There are some rough moments for the CGI too. Overall its not a very good movie.

title: Major League
review: Hilarious baseball comedy, Wild Thing entrance is classic.

title: Wander
review: Pretty bad... bunch of murder illuminati conspiracy bullshit that is bogged down by an overpowering score and whatever fucking voice Aaron Eckhart is trying to do. At least Dr. Molly Clock is in this she's fun, but yeah nothing of note here except a mishandled "cause" and a poor concept to begin with.

title: Marathon Man
review: Strange movie but I liked it. Had a couple of terrifying moments, but I think it missed on its overall ideas.

title: The Sound of Music
review: One of my Mom's favorites. Would be great if it wasn't 3 hours but has some great songs.

title: Yes, God, Yes
review: Brings me back to catholic high school. Fuck catholic high school. Cute and fun movie tho. Pretty much the definition of short and sweet.

title: Rudolph's Shiny New Year
review: The original Rudolf is better. The songs are not very good and it’s pretty forgettable except the Happy baby with big ears. This movie is about trying the end the year and I felt that tho. Someone rescue 2020’s baby so we can be done.

title: The Year Without a Santa Claus
review: Heatmiser and snowmiser songs make it all worth it. Childhood classic.

title: Airplane!
review: Classic, so made great jokes and clever wordplay.

title: Doubt
review:
Wanna watch 4 people (Streep, PSH, Adams, Davis) act for an hour and a half straight with a solid story and strong symbolism? Then this is the movie for you. Very contained story that boils down to 5 great scenes. 

Streep, Adams and PSH in the office
PSH and Adams in the courtyard
Davis and Streep on a walk
Streep and PSH in the office
Streep and Adams in the courtyard

These 5 scene make of the real meat of the movie and show of it's strong writing and acting performances.

title: Moneyball
review: My comfort movie

title: The Girl from Parma
review: This movie has an amazing score and is shot beautifully with great transition especially for 1963. The lead actress is so pretty its almost unfair, and the story is also very ahead of its time with themes of sex and promiscuity. The film does a great job showing the struggle of being an attractive women with the constant pestering of men and having to rebuff unwanted affection and deal with being branded a whore just for doing what she wants which is to eat, sleep and have sex and honestly who can blame her lol. The subtitles were a little fast for me at times but I enjoyed the Italian aesthetic.

title: The Highwaymen
review: Recommended to me by my friend Mike and its the exact type of movie he likes. Its okay but I never really found myself very into it. Also its not a Bonnie and Clyde movie if they don't get absolutely blasted to pieces at the end by Tommy Guns so I'm glad its got that. Also I watched it on 1.25x speed cause I was having trouble getting through it, but I do think that takes a little away from the experience especially in some of the tension building scene.

title: A Few Good Men
review: Just one of the best movies of all time.

title: About Time
review: Its cute :) I didn't really like how much it jumped around, but I guess that make sense for a time travel movie. Has a good heart and Rachel McAdams who is always great.

title: Ava
review: Bad. Done a million and half times before story wise and the action is pretty garbage. Just watch Atomic Blonde its got a better execution of this conceit. At least the actors in this movie are good.

title: Mank
review: Not a huge fan. Had a couple good scene and I liked the old timey film reel style but the movie was mostly confusing. I'm tired of non-linear style especially when it contributes nothing new to the idea like this one does. The acting is great though and I love me some Amanda Seyfried.

title: The Rider
review: Saddest movie I've seen since Manchester by the Sea. I liked it a lot and really give good perspective on life. Has some nuanced metaphors too.

title: Without a Clue
review: Fun twist on some classic Sherlock shenanigans. Michael Caine is amazing and the acting is great all around. One "twist" is fairly predictable but other than that it has a few good surprises.

title: Blow Out
review: Cool movie. Travolta is actually very good and that ending reveal is something else I loved it. Sound design is sick.

title: A Little Princess
review: Its cute but also relies on a lot of kids movie clichés and clichés in general like fucking amnesia. Also she hugs the bully at the end despite them never having a nice moment together which I did not get.

title: Nimic
review: I mean its well shot... but yeah this is stupid. Only 13 minutes tho but 13 minutes I'll never get back.

title: We're the Millers
review: did not laugh much.

title: Prospect
review:
The creators of the Mandalorian saw this movie and said "great concept, but what if we make Pedro Pascal wear a mask the whole time, and make the girl baby yoda?"

This is a cool sci-fi movie with amazing atmosphere and good acting. Pedro Pascal could smooth talk his way out of anything its so soothing. Quick fun watch I recommend.

My criticism would be that for the first half of the movie every line of dialogue sounds like utter nonsense and story is pretty 1 beat. Plays more like an episode of the Mandalorian than it does a feature film, but still very entertaining.

title: The Peanut Butter Falcon
review: Enjoyed it a little less than the first time I watched it just cause the wrestler ending is kinda boring. The Outer Banks adventure aspect of this movie is great though. Still a solid recommend its a fun movie, kind of like Redneck Gifted (2017) in a way

title: Shattered Glass
review: I know Hayden Christensen is amazing in this movie because I want to punch this lying ass in the face the entire time. Peter Saarsgard is also amazing the amount of total bullshit he puts up with in this movie. It's really good and intentionally misleading at times which really emphasizes the point of the story.

title: The Truman Show
review: not much to say its a good movie and everyone knows it

AMC was showing this in theaters again so I decided to go see because it's a great theater movie. So many amazing shots in this movie all set up by the longshot style. One that stood out for me was the shot where they hear the dogfight in the background and then both turn their heads and the camera pans to follow. Just a cool idea executed pretty much perfectly. You know its especially good because there are several moments in this movie where you can forget it's even a longshot. The Poor Wayfaring Stranger song is hauntingly beautiful along with the movies principal metaphor with trees and life. Great movie and fuck that rat.

title: Alita: Battle Angel
review: This was garbage. Looks like a video game most of the time and has a stupid plot and terrible writing all the way through. They try to make Alita this badass but also a naïve at the same time and it’s just makes me cringe. Also it’s obsessed with just saying random numbers like “I work on farm 22” or “I’m hunter warrior 23345!” So dumb. At least the end is somewhat different but still it’s not fun or satisfying.

title: Rushmore
review: Not bad but I have a hard time emotionally connecting to Wes Anderson characters because they are so strange.

title: High Life
review: Interesting concept and well acted but a lot of this movie is just zzzzzzzz with pacing. Also some characters are left rather underdeveloped and it makes some of their actions confusing. I think the nonlinear structure is this movies’ biggest problems and it’s annoying in this movie because it kills tension and instead of creating it. A couple head scratching sound design choices too, overall very meh.

title: Logan Lucky
review: Good movie, added star for rewatchability. It really is Ocean’s 7/11 but has way more heart because of the father daughter relationship and other family aspects.

title: The Kid Detective
review: I was a really big fan of this honestly. It's funny, has a solid story and good character development. I guessed the killer in the second act but by pure dumb luck lol cause the movie encourages you to. The running joke of him not knowing what day it is is fantastic along this scene in the middle of the movie that would be interesting to see again. Big recommendation one the best of 2020.

title: Borat Subsequent Moviefilm: Delivery of Prodigious Bribe to American Regime for Make Benefit Once Glorious Nation of Kazakhstan
review: Lmao the ending had me dead. Genius, comedic and timely movie

title: The Life Aquatic with Steve Zissou
review: Best Wes Anderson movie I've seen so far I think, probably his funniest movie but also the least in his style. The movie does struggle a little with making you care about the emotional crux that is the father-son relationship, but I think it does pull it off pretty well in the end. The large cast of crazy characters make this movie lots of fun plus some of the recurring jokes like the Dolphins are hilarious.

title: mid90s
review: Pretty good movie. Balances emotion and comedy pretty well although some of the emotion is a little raw. Also of course the character in this movie named "Fuckshit" fucks like shit lmaooooo.

title: Scream
review: Pretty good slasher flick. Has nice meta comedy and lots of fun characters. Pretty comical when the girl gets crushed in the cat door, but all I'm saying is that's where the beer was and nobody came to get more for like 45 minutes. Also my popcorn finished at the exact same time as the movie's and that was pretty hype. Good October movie.

title: The New Mutants
review: Its okay. I like the cast but there is not a lot of groundbreaking stuff. Anya Taylor-Joy wears space buns for a good portion of the movie tho and that was worth the price of admission itself. The story is okay but struggles to really find itself at points and kinda has a disconnect between scenes. Some dull moments but held my attention for the whole runtime. The action is a little bit of a CGI mess too, but at least there is some new concepts with it.

title: O Brother, Where Art Thou?
review: Boy does a lot happen in this movie and boy does not much of it make sense. I was entertained thought has funny dialogue and wacky characters. The Soggy Bottom Boys are fire too.

title: Hubie Halloween
review: Watched the first 20 minutes and it’s fucking ASS. Fuck you Sandler this shit is embarrassing

title: The Lost Boys
review: Wasn’t really paying attention but enjoyed the parts where I was. Classical 80s babe too

title: Tenet
review: No idea what happened but it was amazing. It’s tough to hear a lot and you won’t understand anything but I still enjoyed it a ton. The Time Pincer attack is something so unique and insane that only Nolan could have come up with it. I need to watch this movie at least 6 more times but this was a holy experience in IMAX. Nolan legit said “I want a Yacht, a jumbo jet and 5000 extras” and the studio was like yea go for it man.

title: Enola Holmes
review: Narratively it's a mess, breaks the 4th wall whenever it feels like it, dances in and out of narration when ever it's convenient and doesn't show any actual detective work just yells it in your face. The acting is fine, although Millie Bobby Browns crying in one scene is pretty laughable. Tewkesbury is a stupid name and sounded more stupid every time it was said, almost makes you forget how dumb a name Enola is. There is like one well written scene in this whole movie and Enola isn't even in it.

title: The Clovehitch Killer
review: I liked it. Good mystery and solid main characters. The ending was a little messy, but decent use of dual narratives to heighten the tension during the climax.

title: Us
review: Like Jordan's Peele's other movie it has very good re-watchability because of all the subtle hints and foreshadowing. Winston Duke's character is the best but all of the family is doing great acting. I still don't fully understand the metaphor between the tethered and the normal people but it still has a lot of powerful meaning... I think. Nice tension building but there is quite a few jump scares.

title: Ford v Ferrari
review:
What a normal person says when hearing a proposal they like are intrigued by: elaborate

What Henry "the Deuce" Ford II says: *Expand*

title: The Lighthouse
review: God I wish I was that seagull

title: Get Out
review: Absolute masterpiece. Every time I watch it again I notice 50 different details. The coolest one I noticed this time was when Chris first wakes up in the TV room, the first thing he notices is the bouche balls. The deer metaphor is so good and disturbing at the same time. Great great movie.

title: The Devil All the Time
review: I was a pretty big fan of this. Tom Holland is fantastic and it's fun to root for his character the whole movie. There is nothing show stopping and its pretty gruesome at points but overall a very good movie. The narration was a little unnecessary but I didn't mind it too much.

title: The Package
review:
The is probably the best possible movie you could make where the premise is "guy cuts his own dick off" 

It's not that bad and made me laugh a couple times but very predictable. Also this kid smacks his back on the water when cliff jumping and I've done that before and it's not fun.

title: Bill & Ted's Bogus Journey
review: Wasn't very good. Throws out it's fun time travel concept and jokes for some trip through heaven and hell. Very strange and not very good. Wonder if in the third one they will actually have Bill and Ted any different or it's just gonna be a lot more of woahhhhh and dudeeeee.

title: Ocean's Twelve
review: Still very entertaining but in reality it's just a complete rehash of the first movie. Lots of made up heist names, unsurprising twists and an annoying French guy. It's still fun cause of all the fun actors hamming it up but the Julia Roberts pretending to be Julia Roberts hit with Bruce Willis was a little fucking overdone.

title: The Man Who Killed Hitler and Then the Bigfoot
review: This is just a non-fiction documentary about the guy who killed Hitler and Then Bigfoot. It's strange because it's not a giant action thriller with insanity and time travel with you would expect from the name. Has lots of surprising somber beats and melancholy moments. It does paint the main character as a Chuck Norris type figure the way he interacts with everyone, so direct and commanding. The strange beard shaving thing I didn't get either. I would recommend it tho just be prepared for a fucking gruesome fight with Bigfoot (fuck you Bigfoot).

title: Moneyball
review:
One of my favorites. It's a movie about baseball and computers how could I not like it. The Sorkin dialogue and great performances by both Brad Pitt and Jonah Hill make this the best baseball movie without a doubt. Billy Beane's motivations are reasoning are so well defined, one of main reasons I like Sorkin is his characters always act and speak with a purpose. 

"How can you not be romantic about baseball"

"It's a shame that you think we need to explain ourselves. We don't"

Also the ending is the best always makes me tear up a little.

title: Spider-Man: Into the Spider-Verse
review:
Great movie. Hilarious and has actual comic book style. Great soundtrack and lots of fun Easter eggs to enjoy.

title: The Hateful Eight
review: I've heard recently that this was pretty a underrated Tarantino Movie and I'd have to agree. The characters are complex and change in a classic Tarantino style with each reveal of new information. The chaptered  structure and and non-linear style remind me if other good movies like The Ballard of Buster Scruggs and Bad Times at the El Royale. The film is more similar to the ladder with the way each story beat connects another piece of the puzzle. The Jellybean detail is what really got me. Walton Goggins is amazing in this movie. Easiest the most fun character the way he come around to protect justice despite his questionable heritage. Lots of genuine twist and things that legitimacy shocked me see the seemingly long runtime movie effortlessly. There a little much gore/vomiting for me and its one of the most vulgar movies you will ever see but endless action and entertainment. The nailed door is also classic.

title: I'm Thinking of Ending Things
review: I enjoyed it. Very metaphorical and confusing at points but has deep meaning when truly analyzing it. Perfect movie for a stormy night.

title: Baby Driver
review: Got the jams, the action and the fire characters. Everything about this movie is fun and entertaining idk how anyone could not like it. This shit is bananas

title: Get Duked!
review: This was pretty trash. The character are almost like Ed Edd and Eddy parodies and the villains are the least threatening killers I've ever seen. Dumb cop sub-plot but not the fun kind it's just filler. Music is okay, very rough around the edges. The acid scenes are fun I guess.

title: In My Room
review: Quick short film (20 min) I watched on Mubi. Has some cool shots, but there is not any substance to it. Good music too.

title: Insomnia
review: Trying to round out my Nolan movies and this one was pretty damn good. Cool setting and an interesting moral dilemma as the main theme. Not Nolan's typically movie because he didn't write it but the directing is still top notch. Also the acting is good all around. The three leads and minor characters are all great. Feels a little 90's with the "villain calls hero and talks menacing over the phone"

title: Due Date
review: Watched this cause My friend it on, it pretty trash. Galifianakis‘ character is legit just a stupid and terrible person. He deserved it when RDJ spit on his dog and that says a lot.

title: Overlord
review:
Very quality film. Great opening and characters. The story is fun and suspenseful. Also has one of the best trailers I've ever seen like for real it pretty much delivers on all its promises. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=USPd0vX2sdc

Adding a star for good re-watch ability. Also has a line I really like.

"I'm gonna win this one"

title: Seeking a Friend for the End of the World
review: This might be my favorite romance movie ever. Lets start with the concept, it's great. To be honest I think it would be hard to mess this concept up, but they still do an excellent job with it. Good mix of comedy and realism. TV and Radio fill in the gaps well and you get a wide range of human reactions/good moments. Shout out to the dog named "Sorry" thought that was clever and funny. The real pièce de résistance of this movie is the two main characters. Both characters grow tremendously and have great setup and motivations. The best scenes in this movie are between Steve Carell and Keira Knightley and they can say just as much with looks as they do with words it's amazing. The movie manipulates silence, music, and emotion so well. Martin Sheen is also good in his small role. Nothing else to say but I loved, can't believe its not rated higher and thank you to Emma for the recommendation.

title: Joint Security Area
review: Awesome movie. Best part about this movie is that it's shot spectacular. Consistent use of tracking/zoom shots that create tension and build the environments, while also using jump cuts to relieve tension and transition between narratives. Great use of dynamic shots which is popular in Korean cinema and good use of a non-linear story. The story is awesome mostly due to some amazing characters. Themes of friendship, trust, and nationalism on full display. Korean movies are da bomb

title: Taxi
review: Very intriguing and complex look into Iranian cinema. Used just 2 cameras the whole film but very effectively. All the actors are un-credited to protect them, but they all do a great job portraying these real people. His niece is the star of the show, her innocence towards film provides insight to many on the central themes of the movie. None of the passengers are related in any way yet they all contribute to the movie's narrative in a comprehensive way. This storytelling style makes for a chaotic and fast paced but meaningful story. The ending shot with the rose on the dashboard is perfection. Excellent movie.

title: Bill & Ted's Excellent Adventure
review: This movie is most hilarious dudes! Its a good time, lots of funny historical jokes and time travel shenanigans. Its short and sweet, has lots of hot babes and quality references. Interested to see what the sequel is gonna bring to the table.

title: Anastasia
review: Maybe Disney's best animated movie now and they didn't even make it. It looks amazing, has great songs, is historically based and has a cute dog. That my friends is a recipe for a great movie. Anastasia is my skinny independent princess and I love her. Basically I wanna be Dmitri.

title: Thunderstruck
review: I mean its bad but its not THAT bad. Durant is just not a very good actor which besides having a typical sports movie plot is this movie's biggest problem. Also the high school team had a tall black kid that could dunk the whole time but somehow skinny ass Conner was the best kid on the team? I laughed a couple time but yeah not that great.

title: Charlie's Angels
review: This is pretty okay. Thought it ruined it's twist at one point but then saved it by making it a double twist. The angels in this a pretty entertaining and the music make for some pretty enjoyable sequences. Action is decent, plot is pretty linear but solid, but the main reason to watch this is the actresses.

title: Pain & Gain
review:
This movie was pretty fun. Just an absolutely absurd movie with hilariously stupid characters and a plot that will make you question the "based on a true story" fact several times. Honestly this is the perfect movie for Michael Bay to direct and he does a good job. The tracking shots through all the broken holes is a pretty decent visual trick, and the narration fits this movie's style well. My one complaint is it feels like the movie does run a little long despite it being only 2 hours so slight pacing issues. Also this is quotable as hell, I'll drop a few of the best ones...

"Why'd you make me do that to you, Victor? I have responsibilities! Jesus Christ himself has blessed me with many gifts! One of them is knocking someone the fuck out!"

"In the end after reviewing our past performance, we could come to only one conclusion. We're so much better when we wing it."

"Sometimes God just fucks up your order and you gotta chow down on that shitty shame sandwich."

title: Project Power
review: Pretty bad run of the mill action flick. At least Jamie Foxx gets to do his say some menacing shit routine which is always fun. A predictable plot, below average action, and a mediocre concept to begin with did in this movie. Decent use of a rap soundtrack tho

title: Bliss
review: This movie is terrible dude wtf. Definitely should have done drugs before watching this but even then the amount of bullshit and garbage in here is intense. Like the painting turned out pretty cool I guess but you never know what the fuck is going on, every seen looks pretty much identical and nothing that you see matters. Manages to get more bizarre and more boring as it goes on and moves away from reality.

title: Spree
review:
I really liked this more than I should have but it just captures the absurdity and pitfalls of social media so well. The scary thing is people like this actually exist. I used to know this kid lived like 2 streets away from me and he has a Youtube Channel just like Kurt's called flyguyee, here I'l link it https://www.youtube.com/user/flyguyee/videos. He's deleted most of his psychopath one's since but he used to have a video where he claimed he was immune to acid and other where he took his family's new keyboard out into the yard and chopped it with an ax. So anyway this guy ended up making bomb threats to the school and had to go to juvy and he's one of the more tame ones. 

But anyways back to this movie, the types of people this movie portrays are all so extreme yet realistic. Another thing the movie nails is the live chat, the emoji's and the donations are all so on point. I even saw a comment that just said "monkaW" and it's that kind of attention to detail that make a movie so enjoyable. There is a surprising decent message for this movie having a homicidal maniac as it's main character. Had lots of fun with it.

title: Doctor Sleep
review: Very much enjoyed this. Kept me awake on my flight when it was super tired so you know it’s pretty entertaining. Think it does a good job of not trying to be “The Shining 2” and instead just does it’s own thing. Kind of like a superhero film at parts but has interesting themes of alcoholism and grief.

title: Sister of Mine
review: The camerawork in this movie is awesome and some great acting performances especially by Ivana Baquero. However, the movie suffers from the same flaw that a lot of low budget foreign/indie films do and that's a weird/messed up plot. And by that I mean incest, which I probably should have guessed by the title. Other than that I enjoyed the movie, still fucked up and a little dark tho.

title: Jurassic Park
review: Classic movie. Nothing to say but it's great, quotable as hell and well directed.

title: Animal Crackers
review:
Was not a huge fan but it's a fine animated kids film I guess. The animation is kinda gross and lifeless when compared to something like Pixar. (unfair comparison I know) 

The main characters are fine but no real nuance to them, especially the villains. It is what it is

title: 22 Jump Street
review: Stupid but funny. Good how they parody a lot of the traps comedy sequels fall into, pretty much just as good as the first.

title: Star Wars: The Last Jedi
review: I really like most of this movie. Rey, Ben, and Luke tell maybe the most nuanced and interesting Star Wars story of all time. Def the best newer Star Wars movie, even better than Rouge One. This movie does such much right and has so many awesome moments, but is really dragged down by two major problems. One of the main problems is Rose. Her themes and motivations are so archaic in this never Star Wars movie. “Saving what we love, not destroying what we hate” is something you would see in an older Star Wars movie and is out of place considering all this movie does to try and do something new. They should have just stuck with what Finn learns from DJ which I thought was way more interesting. The questionable morals and idea that not everyone is on a “side” opens up way more opportunities creatively IMO. Now the other main problem is JJ Abrams just un-did all the new stuff that Johnson tried to do, including completely contradicting the truth about Rey’s parents. Just so infuriating to see all this movies efforts to do something new and move away from the typical Star Wars stories just ruined by the next one. title: Archive
review: I was a big fan of this. Now I know what you're gonna say this movie is just ripping off "Ex Machina," but actually it's just ripping off "Upgrade." Lots on fun sci-fi in here and the kinds that is right up my alley, this new wave the tech centralized stories like Devs, Ex Machina and Black Mirror just push all the right buttons for me. This movie does have shocking similarities to Ex Machina at first with how they both take place in these isolated and beautiful environments,; The major difference is this movie's ending. Now the real crux of the story is the ending because it changed how you view the film entirely. I've seen this kind of storytelling be criticized before like in Life of Pi how they leave the fantastical details of the story up to interpretation. However in Archives case there are lots of small hints and confusing questions that are answered by the new perspective the ending gives. This to me is an example of strong writing and reminds of the excellent Black Mirror episode "San Junipero," when revealing new information clarifies old information.

title: Arctic
review:
Very cool survival movie, totally nails the realism aspect with this harsh and changing environment. Another highlight is where melting snow and the promise of spring just spawns another challenge by throwing him onto his own 127 hours (more like minutes for him) situation. 

Has slight issues filling it's runtime at points, and the lack of dialogue leaves lots of information up to interpretation. Also I just want to note, the protagonist spends a shocking little amount time trying to come up with a solution to pulling up the woman the cliff. Like this act legit saves him from having to go 2.5 time farther. He just tries to use brute strength and doesn't try any clever idea like a pulley or a counterweight. 

I did however like the last gamble he makes of burning his coat to try and get the attention of the helicopter. Showed that he was truly committed to either living with this woman, or dying with her.
